what: Lottie is kept paused, then while scrolling, when the top edge of the panel (or the section chosen with watch) is below the top of the screen and above 200px from the bottom, it plays once from the start and stays on the last frame — in the section where the full-screen logo flickers into place as letter pieces

options.src: Lottie — JSON URL or #id (inside the document <script type="application/json">)
options.offset: How many px above the bottom of the screen it must rise to trigger, default 200
options.watch: Looks at the top edge of this selector’s nearest ancestor (when playing two logos together in one section), default itself
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Where the Lottie is drawn (child, or itself if none)
options.on: With load, it fires once when the document has fully loaded (window load) without waiting for scroll — the hero logo (#kv_anim_1 on the first page of a reference project). By default it checks the top edge of the panel on scroll

note: Measured only on scroll like the original — if it is already in range from the start, it needs one scroll to run. With reduced motion, it settles on the last scene

from.where: index.html .pl-logo-anime (English·Korean logo assembly, Lottie 50fps 2s, when the section top is within window height − 200)

shared.js [data-cat] (four cat Lottie animations — set up with loop: true, autoplay: false, then play once the top edge of the panel reaches the bottom of the screen (offset: 0, 200 for the cat in the expert section) and keep looping)

index.html .ofk-kv__lottie (offset 150 — original scrollTop > …board top − window height/1.2) · works.html hero (on: load) — original bodymovin loadAnimation svg autoplay false, kv_anim_1 plays on load, kv_anim_2 plays on scroll. Lottie is baked in place by shared.js with the skin colors and put into #ofk-kv-json.
